card.name: Predicting "spot-on" or "correct"
card.fires_on: The word right before an expected "spot-on", "on target" or "correct" judgment, such as "is", "was", "proved" or "spot" after a claim about accuracy. It also fires on "spot" itself in "spot-on".

modes.label: The word spot in spot-on
modes.description: The word "spot" itself, starting the phrase "spot-on" meaning exactly right.

modes.label: Verb or adverb before correct
modes.description: A verb or adverb just before an accuracy word like correct, accurate or on the right track.
modes.example: Their hunch<< proved>> correct. In collaboration with scientists at Baylor

card.writes: It pushes the model to output "spot" (as in spot-on), and away from chemical name pieces like amino and methyl.
card.plain: It lights up when a sentence is about to say something was exactly right, as in "spot-on" or "proved correct".
